Ms.Priti Keshwani, learned counsel for respondent No.
 ORDER

The appellant has filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 08.12.2023 passed by learned I Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhabua (M.P.) in MACC No.122/2020, challenging the quantum of compensation.

entities.text: I Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhabua (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 17.03.2020 at around 1:30 PM, the appellant was going along with his son on a motorcycle bearing registration number MP-45-ML-7441 towards Kaydavad on the Indore- Ahmedabad road.

At that time, when he was entering the road, a car bearing registration number MP-09-CG-4850 came from the Indore side and being driven in a rash and negligent manner by respondent No.1, dashed into the motorcycle of the appellant.
As a result, the appellant sustained grievous injuries on his right leg, right hand and other parts of the body.

He was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32348 2 MA-2195-2024 rushed to Jabhua hospital in an ambulance, where he was given primary treatment and thereafter referred to Saifi Orthopaedic Hospital, Dahod.
In the accident, it was found that the tibia and fibula bones of his right leg had suffered compound fractures and there was a fracture of the femur bone in his right hand.
2.1 The appellant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained.
The Claims Tribunal after recording evidence, concluded that the accident occurred due to the fault of the insured vehicle and accordingly awarded total compensation of Rs.17,65,867/-.

The Tribunal while quantifying the compensation, treated the permanent disability of the appellant as 25%, although the permanent disability certificate (Ex.
P-269) indicated it to be 80%.
3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the reduction of the extent of permanent disability Somla vs Sunil on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193430366/
1 to 25% is incorrect in view of the fact that the appellant has suffered amputation of his right lower limb above the knee.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though the Tribunal has mentioned that the amputation was below the knee,
the evidence on record shows that it was above the knee.
Thus, the assessment of permanent disability at 25% is not justified.

The doctor certified the permanent disability at 80% for which Ex.
P-269, the permanent disability certificate was brought on record.

The expert evidence of Dr.Kavsar Petrolwal, who was examined before the Tribunal also confirms that the appellant has suffered permanent disability, for which the aforesaid certificate was issued by him.
It has further been submitted that, in view of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32348 3 MA-2195-2024 the amputation of the leg, the compensation awarded under other heads is very meagre.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that there is a complete absence of loss of earning due to the permanent disability suffered by the appellant.
She further submits that the appellant failed to prove his income by leading any evidence before the Tribunal.
She submits that as per para 15 of the impugned award, the appellant himself has admitted in para 16 of his cross-examination that he is still receiving salary of Rs.45,000/- per month.
It has further been stated that earlier he was receiving Rs.42,000 to 43,000/- per month.
In para 17 of his cross examination, he has admitted that the department has continued his employment.
4.1 In view of the same, the Tribunal considered the loss of income at Rs.15,000/- per month, which is just and proper.
Hence, she prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
6.

From a perusal of the record, it is seen that for medical expenses, an amount of Rs.10,80,867/-
has been awarded by the Tribunal; for attender charges and special diet Rs.30,000/-; for conveyance Rs.20,000/-; for pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-, which in the considered view of this Court is a just amount of compensation under all the above heads.
However, considering the amputation of the right lower limb, the reduction of permanent disability to 25% is not correct.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32348 4 MA-2195-2024 7.

In the peculiar facts of the present case, considering the amputation of the right lower limb and in view of the evidence available on record in terms of Ex. P-269, the permanent disability certification as well as the expert evidence of Dr.Kavsar Petrolwala, this Court is of the considered view that the permanent disability should be taken as 40%.
8.

As regard the loss of income, in view of the analysis made by the Tribunal in para 15 and on a consideration of the statement of the appellant, particularly paras 16 and 17 of his cross-examination and the specific admission in para 19, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the quantification of loss of income at Rs.40,000/- per month.
9. In view of the change in the extent of permanent disability to 40%, the compensation for loss of earning capacity has to be re-quantified, which after calculation comes to Rs.9,36,000/-.
The differential amount thus comes to Rs.3,51,000/-.

2 10.

sentences.text: As such, the appellant is now required to be paid an amount of Rs.3,51,000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
11. The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal.
12. It is seen from the record that the appeal has been valued at Rs.3,00,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is directed to pay the deficit court fee within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

If the court fees is not paid within this period, interest shall not apply on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32348 5 MA-2195-2024 enhanced amount of compensation beyond the said period of four weeks.
